## v2 → v3: the round-1 union revision (two disjoint Must-Fixes)

**MF-1 [Alternatives] — the regression fixture reproduced a RESHAPED incident.** The
critic read the real incident file; the orchestrator verified it independently. Two
findings:

- The branch name was wrong everywhere — including this task's own `epm:clarify v1`
  marker. `scripts/issue1336_pooled_split.py` does not exist on `issue-1336`; it lives on
  **`issue-1336-fullcorpora`**. The downstream conclusion (not on `main` ⇒ the fixture must
  be self-contained) is unchanged, but the wrong name meant the real code was never opened
  during planning, which is how the fidelity defect got in.
- §12 A10 claimed both incident shapes are early-exit forms covered by the early-exit rule.
  **False on both.** Real shape 1 (`embed_prompts`, 541-560) early-exits, but the
  statements after the If are a LOWERCASE-callee assignment
  (`model = _load_sentence_transformer(revision)`), a `logger.info`, and an `encode` — no
  import, no capitalized-callee call. The production import sits one frame down inside the
  helper (line 531). The early-exit predicate does not fire; the only trigger was the
  incidental `import numpy as np` inside the TOY branch (547) — backwards-keyed, and gone
  the moment that import is hoisted or the toy goes pure-python. Real shape 2
  (`assert_split`, 703-790) has NO early exit at all: it is a per-check
  `if smoke: logger.info(...) else: raise AssertionError(...)`.

  A future regression could therefore gut real-shape detection while every test stayed
  green — the exact defect class this task exists to prevent, reproduced inside the task's
  own verification.

  v3 corrects the branch name and A10, ADDS two structurally faithful fixtures
  (`_FIXTURE_HELPER_WRAPPED`, `_FIXTURE_IFELSE_DOWNGRADE`) beside the existing pair, and
  resolves the load-bearing choice by **extending the heuristic**: one-level, non-recursive
  module-local lowercase-callee resolution into `has_impl` (`has_gate` deliberately gets
  none). The residual — depth ≥ 2 and cross-module helpers — is pinned as a DOCUMENTED
  false negative in a boundary test, named in §8's risk row and in the rule file's
  best-effort disclosure, with the reviewer lens as the catching arm. Both directions are
  now pinned; neither was before.

**MF-2 [Statistics] — the standing-pin coverage claim was wider than the mechanism.**
§6 criterion 2, §0.0, and §10's durability pin all claimed the new lint check pins every
prose surface the plan touches, but §4.10(A)'s surface list contained no `planner.md` and
no `critic.md` entry, and nothing else pins them (`check_agent_spec_size` is size-only).
A future capsule trim would strip the planner's always-loaded hard-requirement token while
every standing lint stayed green — the #606 silent-strip class the `*_review_lens` family
exists to close. v3 took the widen-the-mechanism option: surfaces 6 and 7 added to the
check, two drop cases added to the parametrized test, and all three prose claims
reconciled to what the mechanism actually does.

**Non-blocking items 1-8 folded** in the same round: explicit per-hit WARN suppression
semantics (§4.10(B) vs test 4); two drifted line refs corrected (`no_flags` chain opens
14973 / closes 15042; grandfather dict entries 12656 / 12690); §9 wall-time widened to
~30 min against the selector's measured record; LESSONS.md added to the
implementation-start re-measure list (43 B headroom is not safe against a concurrent

**Item 9 DECLINED by the planner** (explicitly its call, non-blocking): no implementer-
surface edit. Reason — the mirror duty already reaches the implementer via the LESSONS row

## One apparent lens conflict, resolved by direct evidence (no reconciler)

Statistics called the fixture "structurally faithful to both #1336 shapes"; Alternatives
called it reshaped. The lenses examined different objects — Statistics traced the
classifier against the FIXTURE (correctly: it is internally consistent and the rule fires
on it), Alternatives read the REAL incident file. The orchestrator re-read the real file
and confirmed Alternatives. Recorded here because the disagreement was about a claim, not
a verdict — both lenses returned REVISE — so no reconciler was owed.

## Why no re-critique

Per `.claude/skills/adversarial-planner/SKILL.md` § Phase 3, re-critique fires only on an
original REJECT, a changed hypothesis/core design, un-asked-for new scope, or a planner
disagreement with a Must-Fix. None applies: the verdict was REVISE; the design is
unchanged; the one mechanism change (heuristic extension) was explicitly offered by the
critique as MF-1(d)'s sanctioned option; and the sole declined item was non-blocking and
delegated to the planner by the critique itself.
